brief:
The Guardian editorial board warns that Gaza faces mounting civilian casualties during winter months despite international calls for a ceasefire, arguing that formation of a new Israeli government alone will not end the conflict, the newspaper stated. The editorial questions the viability of existing ceasefire frameworks, asking what constitutes a ceasefire when fighting continues unabated.

The Guardian contends that sustained international pressure remains the essential lever for halting Palestinian deaths in Gaza as cold weather compounds humanitarian suffering in the territory.
dek: The formation of a new Israeli government won’t stop the killing, but sustained international pressure must be applied What do you call a ceasefire when the firing has not ceased?
title: Guardian urges international pressure to halt Gaza deaths as winter deepens
